title: Composition of scalar proper/open mates before total limit
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Use the strict reduction lifts $\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], restricted to the discrete constant ring sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline B$. A strict tower means a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ or its $B$ analogue, with its ordinary derived category [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A superscript $(e)$ retains indices $en$ with composite transitions. Put $T=-\otimes_A B$ on constant-coefficient tower complexes; all finite coefficient objects are regarded as constant integral modules by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

Let $E\subset F\subset L$ be finite coefficient fields with ramification indices $e_{F/E}$ and $e_{L/F}$, so that the simultaneous retained levels are $A_{E,n}$, $A_{F,e_{F/E}n}$, $A_{L,e_{L/F}e_{F/E}n}$. For each coefficient inclusion use the strict proper/open scalar mate $q_\bullet^c$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. Write $T_{J/H,W}=-\otimes_{\mathcal O_H}\mathcal O_J$ on constant-coefficient towers and $\alpha^W:T_{L/F,W}T_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E,W}$ for ordinary tensor associativity. Interpret every tower map on the common retained $L$-tower. Then
$$q_{L/E,\bullet}^c\circ\alpha^Y_{\mathcal T_E^c(M)}
=(\mathcal T_L^c(\alpha^X_M))^{(e_{L/F}e_{F/E})}\circ
(q_{L/F,\bullet,C_{F/E,X}M}^c)^{(e_{F/E})}\circ T_{L/F,Y}(q_{F/E,\bullet,M}^c),$$
with the canonical reassociation between the two nested retained towers. The proper factors are the mates of the pasted pullback/scalar squares and the open factors use the same balancing associator $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes bc$. This is an equality of strict derived-tower transformations, including coefficient actions and augmentations. For an identity coefficient inclusion the transformation is identity under the tensor-unit maps. Completed coefficient ring maps and all finite quotient squares preserve these identities and compositions.

After the finite-free tensor/product maps and cofinal Roos maps, the same equation holds for $\gamma_H=r_e^{-1}\mathsf R(q_{\bullet}^c)\tau$ on the ordinary completed-tensor model: writing $P_H^c$ for integral compact support and $C_{J/H,W}$ for ordinary completed scalar extension,
$$\gamma_{L/E,M}\alpha^Y_{P_E^cM}=P_L^c(\alpha^X_M)\gamma_{L/F,C_{F/E,X}M}C_{L/F,Y}(\gamma_{F/E,M}),$$
and $\gamma_{E/E}=1$. Here the integral $\alpha$ is the ordinary completed tensor associator; the maps relating it to the strict constant-coefficient model are the augmentation-normalized comparisons of [lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-reduction].

proof.text: Write $D=\mathcal O_L$, $e=e_{F/E}$, $h=e_{L/F}$ and abbreviate $E,F,L$ by $0,1,2$. Work throughout on the common quotient diagrams $A/t^n$, $B/t^nB$, $D/t^nD$. Indeed $tD=(\varpi_F^e)D=(\varpi_L^{he})D$ as ideals: unit factors do not change the quotients. Thus these are levels $n,en,hen$ of the full towers. The coefficient-model lemma gives finite freeness for each of $B/A,D/B,D/A$, the constant/completed identifications, and completeness and the same finite-Tor bounds for the intermediate inputs. In the quotient-tower associator lemma take $R=\underline A$, $S=\underline B$, $V=\underline D$, $I_n=t^n\underline A$. Its $J_n,K_n$ are precisely our quotient ideals. Its strict $\beta$ equation identifies the two ways of reducing a successive scalar extension, including the quotient augmentations. We henceforth use these identifications, rather than identifying independently chosen finite derived objects.

proof.text:
Write $b_{ji}:T_{ji,\overline X}j_{!,i}\to j_{!,j}T_{ji,X}$ for the open factors. They are the extension-by-zero balancing maps by the strict-scalar-mate statement. Their composition equation is
$$b_{20}\alpha^{\overline X}_{j_{!,0}M}=j_{!,2}(\alpha^X_M)\,b_{21,T_{10,X}M}\,T_{21,\overline X}(b_{10,M}).$$
In the defining extension-by-zero presheaves, on an object factoring through $X$ both maps take $((x\otimes b)\otimes d)$ to $x\otimes bd$; on the zero values both maps are zero. Passing to the sheafified tensors preserves this equality. The coefficient factors have degree zero, so the termwise formula commutes with cochain differentials without a Koszul sign. It also commutes with every transition, since $\overline{bd}=\bar b\bar d$. The exact open comparison in the strict-scalar-mate statement therefore gives this equation in the derived diagram category.

proof.text:
By definition $q_{ji}=Rp_j(b_{ji})a_{ji}$. Expand the successive composite $q_{21}\,T_{21,Y}(q_{10})$. Naturality of $a_{21}$ for $b_{10}:T_{10,\overline X}j_{!,0}M\to j_{!,1}T_{10,X}M$ rewrites its middle pair as
$$a_{21,j_{!,1}T_{10}M}\,T_{21,Y}(Rp_1b_{10})=Rp_2(T_{21,\overline X}b_{10})\,a_{21,T_{10,\overline X}j_{!,0}M}.$$
Consequently the open factors become $Rp_2(b_{21}\,T_{21,\overline X}b_{10})$ and the proper factors become $a_{21}T_{21,Y}(a_{10})$. Substitute Steps 3 and 4 and use naturality of the tensor associators. The result is exactly
$$q_{20}\alpha^Y=\mathcal T_2^c(\alpha^X)^{(he)}\,(q_{21})^{(e)}\,T_{21,Y}(q_{10}).$$
Here $q_{21}$ is evaluated at $C_{10,X}M$, and restricting its already $h$-retained target at $en$ gives level $hen$. The two successive restrictions have identical objects and composite transitions to restriction by $he$. This proves the first displayed equation of the item before any derived limit. It uses naturality in the diagram category, with no faithfulness assertion for evaluation.

proof.text: For an identity inclusion the pullback/scalar square is identity under multiplication $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$. Its proper mate is identity by clause (4) of the mate-pasting lemma. The open balancing map is the same multiplication on the nonzero extension-by-zero values and the identity on zero. Thus $q_{ii}=1$ under the unit maps. Quotient compatibility in Steps 2--5 is also an equation on diagrams: replacing all coefficients by their images in a further quotient leaves $x\otimes bd$ equal to $x\otimes\bar b\bar d$. The strict mate supplies the corresponding commuting quotient-transition squares, while the quotient-tower associator carries $x\mapsto x\otimes\bar1$ to that same augmentation. The scalar-limit-reduction lemma supplies the augmentation-normalized realization of these maps. Finally the completed coefficient map $R_0\to R_2$ and its two-stage composite have equal projections into every finite $L$-quotient: choose $n$ with $hen\geq a$ for a quotient of level $a$, and use the quotient-ring map induced by the original ring inclusions. Equality of these projections implies equality into the inverse limit defining $R_2$. The identity case is proved by the same projection calculation. This proves the claimed coefficient action, augmentation, identity and completed-map compatibilities.

proof.text:
For a strict tower $K$ put $\tau_{ji,K}:T_{ji}\mathsf R(K)\to\mathsf R(T_{ji}K)$. The horizontal Roos coherence lemma, applied with $F=T_{10}$, $G=T_{21}$, $L=T_{20}$ and the tensor associator $\alpha:GF\to L$, gives the specified equality
$$\mathsf R(\alpha_K)\,\tau_{21,T_{10}K}\,T_{21}(\tau_{10,K})=\tau_{20,K}\,\alpha_{\mathsf R(K)}.$$
These maps are invertible by the finite-free assertion of the cofinality lemma and Step 1. The same cofinality lemma gives naturality of $r_e$ for tower maps, commutation with $\tau$, preservation of the zero shifted-product augmentation, and
$$r_h^{K^{(e)}}r_e^K=r_{eh}^K.$$
For the last formula the selection maps pick $x_{ehn}$ and the successive weighted block sums concatenate the blocks $[ehn,eh(n+1))$, so no factor or sign is introduced on either cone coordinate. These are the actual cochain maps used in the scalar-limit-reduction statement, not arbitrary isomorphisms with a derived limit.

proof.text:
Apply $\mathsf R$ to Step 5 and insert the comparisons of Step 7. To check the resulting composition equation, postcompose both proposed maps into the full $L$-tower limit by its invertible $r_{eh}$. For the direct map $r_{eh}$ cancels its inverse in $\gamma_{20}=r_{eh}^{-1}\mathsf R(q_{20})\tau_{20}$. For the successive route write $r_{eh}=r_e^{(h)}r_h$. Naturality of $r_e$ moves the restriction past $\mathsf R(q_{21})$, and commutation of $r_e$ with $\tau_{21}$ then cancels the factor $T_{21}(r_e^{-1})$ coming from $T_{21}(\gamma_{10})$. What remains, before the target map induced by $\alpha^X$, is
$$\mathsf R((q_{21})^{(e)})\,\mathsf R(T_{21}q_{10})\,\tau_{21,T_{10}U_0}\,T_{21}(\tau_{10,U_0}),\qquad U_0=\mathcal T_E^c(M).$$
Here naturality of $\tau_{21}$ moved it past $q_{10}$. The $\mathsf R$-image of Step 5 and the horizontal $\tau$ equation of Step 7 identify this with the direct expression $\mathsf R(q_{20})\tau_{20}\alpha$. Cancel $r_{eh}$. This proves the composition equation on the constant-coefficient realization. All cancellations occur in the derived category; no inverse cochain map is chosen for $r_e$.

proof.text:
It remains to identify the associators in this equation with the ordinary completed-tensor associators in the item. The coefficient-model lemma identifies complete constant objects with the completed coefficient objects and identifies the ordinary/strict comparisons with the specified $\chi$. Its completeness assertions apply to $M,C_{10,X}M$ and to both compact-support outputs, so the comparisons may all be used here. The scalar-completion-associator lemma states precisely
$$a^I_K\,I_{21}(\chi_{10,K})\,\chi_{21,C_{10}K}=\chi_{20,K}\,a^C_K,$$
where $a^I$ is made from balanced quotient tensors, finite-free tensor/product interchange and cofinal uniformizer replacement. Thus the associator used in Step 8 is the transport of $a^C$, at $X$ and $Y$, through those actual comparisons. The scalar-limit-reduction statement identifies its $\gamma$ with $r_e^{-1}\mathsf R(q)\tau$ preserving the action and augmentation. Conjugate Step 8 by these specified isomorphisms and use the displayed $\chi$ equation on its source and target. This gives the displayed composition equation for $\gamma_{L/E}$ with $P_L^c(\alpha^X_M)$ and ordinary completed $\alpha^Y$. For the identity extension, Step 6, $r_1=1$, the identity comparison in horizontal Roos coherence, and the unit normalization of the scalar-completion associator give $\gamma_{E/E}=1$. All quotient and augmentation equations survive these specified comparisons by the same cited normalization statements.

proof.text: M7 Lean proof of the completed identity clause. The identity-on-sections normalization identifies the composite of two identity scalar restrictions with the restriction functor whiskered with its identity comparison. Exact localization preserves this left-unit equation. The normalized composite-adjunction uniqueness isomorphism agrees with the conjugate associator, so Mathlib leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp identifies compositionCompleted for two identity embeddings with scalar extension applied to compositionUnitCompleted. Evaluate the already proved completed composition equation at two identity embeddings. Naturality of completedArrow at the source tensor unit rewrites its right side. Scalar-limit reduction makes completedArrow invertible on the finite-Tor domain; cancel that component. Scalar extension along the identity coefficient map is faithful because compositionUnitCompleted identifies it with the identity functor. Faithfulness gives precisely completedArrow followed by support of the source unit equals the target unit. No new postponed statement is used. The strict identity and the remaining geometric and Roos composition clauses retain their existing proof plans.

proof.text: Lean reduction of compactSupportScalarLimitComposition: horizontal normalized tensor/limit coherence supplies the alpha/tau square and arithmetic tensor coherence supplies the tau/r square. Ordinary limit.pre_pre and arithmetic index equality, followed by rightDerivedPullback_comp, prove the cofinal composition law. Postcompose both compact-support routes with r_(h*e), use naturality to move the support associator and the second strict arrow through r, cancel the inverse r_h and the scalar image of the inverse r_e, then apply naturality of tau. The remaining equation is scalarLimit applied to compactSupportStrictScalarComposition, preceded by the horizontal tau square. Cancel r_(h*e). This is a decomposition of the limit-composition hole into the two geometry-independent coherence steps, with all categorical glue proved. The four other pre-existing holes remain unchanged.

F7 Lean proof of compositionOpen: apply ordinaryBaseOpenTensor_composition separately at each index of an ordinary strict tower; natural-transformation extensionality gives the ordinary tower equation. The proved localize_scalar_square helper in ConstantCompletedScalarAssociativity carries that equation through exact localization with the specified compositionTowerOrdinary associators. Rewrite all three localized open maps using openTensor_ordinary. Thus no equality of derived maps is inferred merely from evaluation, and the comparison is the original scalar mate. Proper composition, strict support composition and strict identity remain as their original named obligations.

Apply the support-realization coherence theorem to the image-tower comparison equation supplied by compactSupportStrictScalarComparison. The coherence theorem is the support-model, reduction-balancing, and retained-level part of Steps 3--6; the resulting equation is exactly the displayed compact-support arrow composition.
